Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

'Concerning the MERCIFUL AND MEEK ONE who is to come in the latter time, who shall avenge himself against the cruel and deceiving Devil... the islands of Egypt rejoice.' One of the MOST DISTINCTIVELY MESSIANIC LINES in the trilogy. 'The merciful and meek one (ቸርና የዋህ) who is to come in the latter time' echoes MATTHEW 11:29 ('I am meek and lowly of heart') and the standard Christian-era messianic vocabulary. 'The islands of Egypt rejoice' likely draws on Isaiah 19:18-25 (Egypt and Assyria worship the LORD) — read in Christian patristic tradition as PROPHECY OF COPTIC AND AKSUMITE CHRISTIANITY. *Philological caveat (per Horovitz 1905 p. 196 + CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §62):* Horovitz noted 'von Christus nirgends die Rede' — there is nowhere any talk of Christ in Meqabyan, which he understood as deliberately OT-framed. The Christological reading at 3 Mq 1:1 is therefore Christian-readerly overlay; a non-Christological messianic reading is fully possible.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

THE SATAN-REFUSED-TO-WORSHIP-ADAM TRADITION — the most diagnostic angelological verse in 3 Meqabyan. The Devil himself states: 'For when I said "I will not bow to my inferior," God for the sake of their father Adam humbled me from my glory.' Found principally in: (a) the Latin VITA ADAE ET EVAE §§12-17 (Pettorelli-Kaestli CCSA 18, Brepols 2012; absent from the Greek Apocalypse of Moses), where Satan tells Adam: 'on your account I was cast out from the heavens... when God blew into you the breath of life, and you were made in the image of God, Michael led you and said to me: Worship the image of God. And I said: I will not worship one inferior to me'; (b) 2 ENOCH 29:4-5 (longer recension J; cf. 31:3-6 linking the fall explicitly to Adam); (c) the QUR'AN seven-passage cluster (Sura 2:34; 7:11-18; 15:28-38; 17:61; 18:50; 20:116; 38:71-78 — Iblis refuses to bow to Adam); (d) the EOTC's CAVE OF TREASURES §2 (Budge 1927; Reeves OR ed.); (e) the proximate Geʽez recipient, the CONFLICT OF ADAM AND EVE WITH SATAN (Dillmann 1853 / Trumpp 1880 / Malan 1882); (f) among Jewish sources, only BERESHIT RABBATI of Moses ha-Darshan (Narbonne, 11th c.; Albeck ed. 1940 pp. 24-25). The verse provides the CANONICAL EOTC EXPLANATION FOR THE ORIGIN OF DEMONIC ENMITY TOWARD HUMANS: Satan was deposed BECAUSE he refused to worship the image of God in Adam.

And I said: I will not worship one inferior to me'; (b) 2 ENOCH 29:4-5 (longer recension J; cf. 31:3-6 linking the fall explicitly to Adam); (c) the QUR'AN seven-passage cluster (Sura 2:34; 7:11-18; 15:28-38; 17:61; 18:50; 20:116; 38:71-78 — Iblis refuses to bow to Adam); (d) the EOTC's CAVE OF TREASURES §2 (Budge 1927; Reeves OR ed.); (e) the proximate Geʽez recipient, the CONFLICT OF ADAM AND EVE WITH SATAN (Dillmann 1853 / Trumpp 1880 / Malan 1882); (f) among Jewish sources, only BERESHIT RABBATI of Moses ha-Darshan (Narbonne, 11th c.; Albeck ed. 1940 pp. 24-25). The verse provides the CANONICAL EOTC EXPLANATION FOR THE ORIGIN OF DEMONIC ENMITY TOWARD HUMANS: Satan was deposed BECAUSE he refused to worship the image of God in Adam.

TRANSITION TO GOD'S-RESPONSE — the Devil's-petition narrative (culminating at 1:15 SATAN-REFUSED-TO-WORSHIP-ADAM) is followed by the divine-response sequence (Ch 2:1 Job-allusion). Ch 1:18 marks the structural-pivot: the Devil's-speech ends + God's-judicial-response opens. The dialogical-structure parallels: JOB 1-2 (Satan-petition + divine-permission); 1 KINGS 22:21-23 (the lying-spirit's-petition + divine-commission); REVELATION 12:7-12 (the cosmic-battle-and-defeat with antiphonal-heavenly-response). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the divine-response is not punitive-judgment but THEODICY-VIA-JOB-CITATION — Ch 2's working-out of Job's-vindication as paradigm for human-resistance-to-deception. The verse functions as STRUCTURAL HINGE: from Devil-speaks (Chs 1) → to God-speaks (Ch 2) → to homiletic-development of the divine-response (Chs 3-9) → to eschatological-resurrection-capstone (Ch 10).

POST-FALL DIVINE JUDGMENT-PRONOUNCEMENT (vv. 22-25): God's irrevocable verdict on the Devil. The verse parallels: GENESIS 3:14-15 (the curse-on-the-serpent — 'I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel' — the Protoevangelium); EZEKIEL 28:16-19 (the king-of-Tyre / Satan-fall judgment-pronouncement — 'I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God; I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire'); ISAIAH 14:15 (Lucifer's-fall — 'thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit'); REVELATION 12:9 + 20:10 (the final-defeat). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the judgment is DELIVERED VIA THE DEVIL'S OWN PETITION (Ch 1 first-person speech) — the rebel arrests-and-condemns himself by his own argumentation. Tewahedo theology preserves this self-incrimination as the paradigm for unrepentant-sin (4:34 complete-repentance contrast).

CHAPTER-CLOSING TRANSITION — closes the chapter's cosmological-introduction sequence. The closing verses likely include a brief doxological-pause before Ch 2's God-response opens. The intra-chapter-closing pattern parallels the standard EOTC homiletic-anthology genre: chapters end with miniature-doxologies preparing the next thematic development (cf. the inner-doxologies of LXX Sirach + Wisdom of Solomon + 4 Maccabees). Tewahedo lectionary tradition preserves the chapter-by-chapter homiletic-reading structure for Säʿatat (Liturgy of the Hours). The verse closes the Devil's-hubris-and-fall narrative — the longest sustained-Devil-first-person-speech section in EOTC canonical literature — and prepares the transition to the divine-response architecture of Ch 2. The Devil-speaks pattern is suspended; the homiletic-mode shifts to God-speaks for the chapter-break.
